body.p: Claims 1-12 are pending in the present application and are rejected. By this response, claims are amended as indicated. Claims 13-20 are added. No claims are cancelled. No new matter is added.

Although the present communication includes alterations to the application or claims, or characterizations of claim scope or referenced art, Applicant is not conceding in this communication that previously pending claims are not patentable over the cited references. Rather, any alterations or characterizations are being made to facilitate expeditious prosecution of this application.
Reconsideration of the present application as amended based on the arguments set forth hereinbelow is respectfully requested.
Claims 1-3 and 5-12 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 102(a)(1) as allegedly being anticipated by U.S. Pat. No. 7,578,477 to French et al. (hereinafter, "French").
This rejection is respectfully traversed.

Regarding the rejection of claim 1, Applicant respectfully notes that the Examiner alleges the "front plate 26" of French is analogous to the claimed "internal panel." Further, the Examiner alleges that claim this "front plate 26" in French is "subjected to pressurization," citing to col. 4, lines 1-5 of French for alleged support. Applicant respectfully notes that French describes how it is vital that, in the event of a depressurizing event on either side of the "second door 12" (which is the structure shown in FIGS. 2 and 3 thereof), "means permit the automatic opening of this door so as to balance the pressures between cabin 14 and cockpit 2 and thus prevent excessive stress on the aircraft structure." (French, col. 4, lines 1-4.)

Applicant respectfully submits that French discloses, in essence, that the "second door 12" actively resists a pressure gradient being present on opposite sides thereof. In French, "[i]llustrations 5 to 8 show the behavior of panels 18 when

a [depressurization event] occurs in the front of the airplane, ... on the side of the front face of second door 12." (Id., col. 5, lines 3-6.) In this circumstance, "[s]econd door 12 is designed in such a way that panels 18 give away and are sucked inside aisle 8." (Id., col. 5, lines 9-11.) French further describes that "[i]llustrations 12 to 14 show how air can circulate from the front to the back of the plane through second door 12." (Id., col. 7, lines 12-13.) For this purpose, "check valves" are disclosed in French as being provided in the "second door 12" and are used for multiple purposes, among them being "to permit ventilation to the area reserved for the crew and served by aisle 8," "during the closing of second door 12 to prevent over-pressurizing the aisle [8]," and also "in the event of a [depressurization event] inside cabin 14," in which case "air can pass from aisle 8 to cabin 14." (Id., col. 7, lines 50-56.)

With this functionality of the door of French established, Applicant respectfully submits that the Examiner's interpretation of the phrase "to be subjected to pressurization" is not commensurate with the intended scope of the claims in the instant application. Indeed, the Examiner's interpretation renders the claim language at issue almost meaningless since, in French, the "panels 18" of the "second door 12" are literally blown off the door frame (shown sequentially in FIGS. 6 and 7 of French) in the case of a depressurization of the "cockpit 2" and are provided with check valves that readily allow passage of air through the "second door 12" in the case of a depressurization of the "cabin 14."

Thus, while Applicant does not agree with the Examiner's interpretation of this "to be subjected to pressurization" claim language, Applicant has nevertheless elected to amend this claim language in an attempt to advance prosecution of the instant application. As currently amended herein, the "aircraft fuselage door" comprises "a movable internal panel configured to create a seal between an inside and an outside of an aircraft to which the aircraft fuselage door is attached and to allow a passenger cabin of the aircraft to be pressurized...." Support for this amended claim language can be found throughout the instant application as filed, including at least, for example, on p. 8, lines 12-16. No new matter is added. Applicant respectfully submits that, since the "second door 12" of French is

designed to prevent the formation of a pressure differential on opposite sides thereof, it cannot reasonably be alleged that the "second door 12" of French is "configured to create a seal between an inside and an outside of an aircraft to which the aircraft fuselage door is attached and to allow a passenger cabin of the aircraft to be pressurized," as recited in currently amended claim 1. Thus, Applicant respectfully asserts that currently amended claim 1 is not anticipated by French for at least this reason.

Applicant further respectfully notes that claim 1 is further amended herein to recite that the "aircraft fuselage door" comprises "a resilient connection between and connecting the external panel and the internal panel to form an internal free space between the internal panel and the external panel, such that the internal panel is movable relative to the external panel...." Claim 1 is also amended herein to recite that "the resilient connection is configured to isolate the external panel from a movement of the internal panel relative to the external panel." In rejecting claim 1, the Examiner alleges that the "rear plate 28" is analogous to the "aerodynamic external panel," which, in order to satisfy the claim language of original claim 1, must be established as "being resiliently connected to the [front plate 26] to form an internal free space between the internal panel and the external panel." The Examiner generally alleges that this feature is shown in FIG. 3 of French, but provides no other support or discussion for this alleged teaching of French.

Applicant respectfully submits that there is no disclosure in FIG. 3 of French, nor in any other part of French, that the "rear plate 28" is "resiliently connected to" the "front plate 26." Applicant respectfully notes that the word "resiliently" in this context means "capable of withstanding shock without permanent deformation or rupture." Applicant respectfully submits that there is no disclosure in French that establishes any analogous connection between the "rear plate 28" and the "front plate 26." Applicant further respectfully submits that there is no disclosure in French of any connection between the "rear plate 28" and the "front plate 26" that renders "the internal panel ... movable relative to the external panel" and/or "isolate[s] the [rear plate 28] from a movement of the [front plate 26] relative to the

[rear plate 28]," as is required according to the plain meaning of currently amended claim 1. Indeed, FIGS. 6 and 7 of French clearly show that, the moment the "front plates 26" begin their pivoting movement, the "spacer 38" is no longer pressed against the internal face of the "rear plates 28," thereby allowing simultaneous pivoting movement of the "rear plates 28" along with the "front plates 26," although this initial pivoting movement of the "rear plates 28" is initially small because the "rear plates 28" are hinged on an opposite end from the "front plates 26."
Thus, Applicant respectfully asserts that currently amended claim 1 is not anticipated by French for at least this reason as well.

Regarding the rejection of claim 5, Applicant respectfully notes that claim 5 is currently amended to provide greater clarity as to the scope of the subject matter intended to be claimed therein. As currently amended, claim 5 recites that the "resilient connection" recited in claim 1 is configured to allow for an opening and closing of the aircraft fuselage door itself by allowing this relative movement between the internal panel and the external panel. As recited in currently amended claim 5, "when the internal panel is moved toward the external panel, coming into contact, at least partially, with the external panel, the resilient connection is configured to allow the internal panel to push the external panel towards the outside of the aircraft, so as to open the aircraft fuselage door;" and "when the internal panel is moved away from the external panel, the resilient connection is configured to pull the external panel with the internal panel, so as to close the aircraft fuselage door." Support for this amended claim language can be found throughout the instant application as filed, including for example, original claim 5 and also from p. 14, line 21, through p. 15, line 7. No new matter is added.

In rejecting claim 5, the Examiner cites to FIG. 8 of French and states that "element 48 allows contact between element 26 and 28." Applicant respectfully submits that, according to French, "link 48 ... may be a cable, a harness, a strip or similar" that "lines from plate 26 to rear plate 48." (French, col. 5, lines 24-26.) As an example, French states that "link 48 is for instance secured to spacer 38 on one side and on wedge 39 on the other side." (Id., col. 5, lines 26-27.) Applicant respectfully submits that such a flexible structure as "link 48," attached and used

in the manner shown and described in French, is not capable of either "allow[ing] the internal panel to push the external panel towards the outside of the aircraft, so as to open the aircraft fuselage door" or "pull[ing] the external panel with the internal panel, so as to close the aircraft fuselage door." Thus, Applicant respectfully submits that French does not anticipate claim 5 for at least this reason.

Regarding claims 2, 3, and 5-12, Applicant further respectfully notes that each of these claims ultimately depends from independent claim 1 and recites additional features to those recited in independent claim 1. Thus, Applicant respectfully asserts that claims 2, 3, and 5-12 are also patentable over French for at least the same reasons as independent claim 1.

For at least these reasons, Applicant respectfully asserts that claims 1-3 and 5-12 are not anticipated by French. Thus, Applicant respectfully requests that the rejection of claims 1-3 and 5-12 under 35 U.S.C. § 102 be withdrawn and that these claims be allowed at this time.

Applicant acknowledges with appreciation the Examiner's statement that, while claim 4 is objected to as depending from a rejected independent claim, this claim nevertheless recites allowable subject matter and would be allowable if rewritten in independent form, including all of the features of the independent claim and any intervening dependent claims. Applicant respectfully submits that, in light of the amendments to claim 1, from which claim 4 ultimately depends, claim 4 is in condition for allowance without the subject matter thereof being rewritten in independent claim form and early notice regarding the allowance of claim 4 is respectfully requested.

New claims 13-20 are added. Support for new claims 13-16 can be found at least, for example, on p. 9, lines 18-20, p. 10, lines 5-10, p. 12, lines 13-17, and in claim 2 of the instant application as filed. Support for new claims 17-20 can be found at least, for example, in original claims 1-6 of the instant application as filed.

No new matter is added. Applicant respectfully notes that each of new claims 13- 16 ultimately depends from independent claim 1 and recites additional features to those recited in independent claim 1. Thus, Applicant respectfully asserts that new claims 13-16 are also patentable over French for at least the same reasons as independent claim 1. Applicant further respectfully asserts that new claim 17, as well as new claims 18-20 that depend therefrom, are in condition for allowance, at least since new claim 17 essentially constitutes claim 4 having been rewritten in independent form, which the Examiner states "would be allowable." Accordingly, Applicant respectfully asserts that new claims 13-20 are in condition for allowance and early notice regarding the same is respectfully requested.
In light of the above amendments and remarks, it is respectfully submitted that the present application is now in condition for allowance, and an early notice to such effect is earnestly solicited.

Applicant does not otherwise concede, however, the correctness of the Office Action's rejection with respect to any of the limitations of the independent claims and dependent claims discussed above. Accordingly, Applicant hereby reserves the right to make additional arguments as may be necessary to further distinguish the claims from the cited references, taken alone or in combination, based on additional features contained in the independent or dependent claims that were not discussed above. A detailed discussion of these differences is believed to be unnecessary in view of the basic differences in the independent claims pointed out above.

If any matter should remain outstanding after the Patent Examiner has had an opportunity to review the above remarks, the Patent Examiner is respectfully requested to contact the undersigned patent attorney in order to resolve these matters and avoid the issuance of another Official Action.
The Office is hereby authorized to charge any additional fees or credit any overpayments under 37 C.F.R. §§ 1.16, 1.17 to U.S. Deposit Account No. 50-6521.
